_readme: Two interactive primary pages: letter formation for Grade 1 and songs for Grade 2.

Grade 1 and Grade 2 share one NIE syllabus, Activity Based Oral English, organised into 16 themes. The songs are chosen to go with those themes; the syllabus names songs to use but the ones here are RCF English's, so each is labelled 'goes with' a theme rather than 'from' it.

SONG WORDS AND TUNES. Four sets of words are written for RCF English and set to traditional tunes that are long out of copyright: Frere Jacques, Row Row Row Your Boat, Mary Had a Little Lamb and Old MacDonald Had a Farm. Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star uses Jane Taylor's words of 1806 and its traditional tune. Do not add a song whose words or tune are still in copyright - The Wheels on the Bus, for example, is a 1939 song and is not free to use.

SONG LINE FORMAT. Each line is space-separated tokens: text:note:beats. Beats are in quarter notes. A token ending in '-' joins the next syllable of the same word; one ending in '=' joins it with a visible hyphen. The build warns on a malformed token.
The generator reads page files as UTF-8, so emoji and accented letters are written directly.

hero.text: Watch each letter being written, one stroke at a time, on the same four lines as a copy book. Then have a go yourself.

blocks.title: How to use the board
text: **1. Watch.** Press *Watch* and follow the pencil point. The numbers show where each stroke starts.
**2. Say it.** Say the letter's name, and the word, with the board.
**3. Air-write.** Draw the letter in the air with a finger, big, in the same order.
**4. Your turn.** Press *Your turn* and trace over the dotted letter. Then write it in a copy book.

blocks.heading: Why the starting point matters
text: A child who starts every letter in the right place and moves the pencil the right way will join letters easily later on. A child who starts at the bottom of an *o*, or draws a *d* as a stick and then a circle, has a habit that has to be unlearned - and unlearning is much slower than learning it right the first time.
That is why the board numbers every stroke and moves a pencil point along it. The finished shape matters less than the way it is made.
bullets: **Most letters start at the top.** Straight lines usually go down, not up.
**Round letters start at the top right and go anticlockwise** - *c, a, d, g, o, q* all begin the same way, so learn *c* first.
**Small letters sit on the red line.** Their bodies reach the dashed middle line; tall letters like *b, d, h, k, l* go up to the top line, and tails on *g, j, p, q, y* drop to the bottom line.

blocks.title: A letter's name is not its sound
text: The board says each letter's **name** - *bee* for B - and a word that starts with it. It does not try to say the letter's **sound** on its own, because a computer voice cannot say a clean /b/ without adding a vowel to it, and a wrong sound is worse than none.

Say the sounds yourself, clipped and short. [Alphabet Practice](primary-english/alphabet/) explains the difference and shows how to practise sounds. The word *fox* is used for X because very few everyday words start with the sound X makes.

hero.text: Five short songs to sing together. Press play, follow the words as they light up, and sing along.

blocks.title: About these songs
text: Grade 1 and Grade 2 share one syllabus, *Activity Based Oral English*, and each of its themes uses songs to teach words and sentence patterns. Each song here goes with one of those themes, so it works in Grade 1 as well.

**The tunes are traditional and very old**, so they are free for anyone to use. The words of *Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star* were written by Jane Taylor in 1806. The words of the other four were written for RCF English.

items.title: Listen first
text: Play the tune once while the children just listen and watch the words light up.

items.title: Say the words
text: Press *Say the words*, or say them yourself, slowly, a line at a time. Children repeat each line.

items.title: Sing slowly
text: Tick *Slower* and sing along. Point to the words as they light up.

items.title: Add actions
text: Wave for *hello*, wiggle fingers for *twinkle*, rub hands for *wash*. Actions help children remember the words.

items.title: Sing it again
text: Untick *Slower* once the song is known. Children love singing a song they know well - repeat it on later days.

blocks.title: About the sound
text: The tune is played as soft, quiet notes made by the browser itself - there are no audio files to download. Nothing plays until you press a button, and the sound switch at the top of the songs turns it off.
**The tune has no singing voice. The children do the singing.** That is what makes it an action song rather than a video to watch.
